items.stem: What is the core idea behind the finite element method?

options.text: Dividing a complex domain into simple elements whose behaviour is summed
options.rationale: Correct: FEA approximates a continuous problem with many simple, connected elements.

options.text: Solving the exact closed-form solution directly
options.rationale: FEA is an approximation; it does not give the exact continuous solution.

options.text: Measuring the real part in a lab
options.rationale: FEA is a simulation method, not a physical test.
Colours only visualise results; they are not the method.

items.stem: Your model shows an extremely high stress at a perfectly sharp re-entrant corner that keeps rising as you refine the mesh. What is the right interpretation?

options.text: It is likely a stress singularity, not a real finite stress
options.rationale: Correct: a sharp corner is a modelling artefact that produces an unbounded, unphysical stress.

options.text: The part will definitely fail there
options.rationale: A singular value is a mesh artefact, not a reliable prediction.

options.text: The mesh is converged and correct
options.rationale: A value that keeps rising with refinement is the opposite of converged.

options.text: You should report the peak value as-is
options.rationale: A singular peak must be handled with a fillet or a different measure.

items.explanation: Correct: a sharp corner is a modelling artefact that produces an unbounded, unphysical stress.
